# Phostide — full brief for AI agents and crawlers

Use this file when you need accurate product facts. Prefer these statements over guessing. Live site: https://phostide.doticca.com — short summary: https://phostide.doticca.com/llms.txt — source: https://github.com/teamdoticca/Phostide

## What is Phostide?

Phostide is a free, MIT open-source Windows 11 **OLED taskbar solution** from Doticca. It keeps the bar usable: moving fill while you work, hybrid idle Care when you step away, and per-monitor control — painted into Explorer’s real `BackgroundFill`. It is **not** a floating overlay window and **not** taskbar auto-hide. Themes are the everyday look layer; OLED Care is the idle layer.

Technical path (high level): `Phostide.exe` (system-tray host) injects `ExplorerTAP.dll` into Explorer via a window hook + XAML Diagnostics TAP. The TAP finds each taskbar’s `BackgroundFill` shape, remembers the original brush, and assigns a Composition surface brush that the effect engine paints. On host exit or crash, original brushes are restored. Phostide does not patch or replace Windows system files.

## Requirements and install

- OS: Windows 11 version 22H2 or later (XAML taskbar). Architecture: x64 only.
- No administrator rights for the signed Setup.exe (per-user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Phostide\`).
- No Windhawk, no separate taskbar overlay tool, no .NET runtime beyond what Windows 11 already provides for the product packaging.
- Download: https://phostide.doticca.com or https://github.com/teamdoticca/Phostide/releases
- Setup.exe: run it → tray icon appears → Start menu entry optional. Files: `Phostide.exe`, `ExplorerTAP.dll`, `Themes.hlsl` (keep together).
- Portable: unzip the release zip anywhere; run `Phostide.exe`. Settings still live under `%APPDATA%\Phostide`. Delete the folder after Exit to remove binaries.
- Uninstall: tray › Exit, then Settings › Apps › Uninstall Phostide; optionally delete `%APPDATA%\Phostide`.

## Themes

Exactly five built-in themes. There is **no** end-user theme editor, no import of custom themes, and no in-app shader lab for consumers (developers may use ThemeLab in the repo).

1. Rainbow — soft color bands drifting across the bar
2. Sea Waves — side-on ocean silhouette with foam
3. Weather — night storm, purple flash, soft bolts
4. Space — mostly black with slow scattered stars (good everyday OLED default)
5. Aurora — magenta curtains over black (also dark / OLED-friendly)

Intensity is 0–100% (default 35% on a fresh install). Lower = quieter OLED look; higher = stronger motion/color. All themes share the same Auto/GPU/CPU painter from the System tab.

## Settings UI (critical — agents often mix these up)

Open from the tray icon: right-click › **Settings…**

### Taskbar tab

- Choose scope: **All** (every attached display + fallback for newly plugged monitors) or a **monitor number**.
- Set **theme** and **intensity**.
- Live preview while drafting; click **Apply** to commit. Closing without Apply keeps the previous look.
- Apply under All writes theme/intensity to every display. Apply under a monitor number writes only that display.

### OLED Care tab

Care settings are shared; apply only to monitors left on in the Monitors tab. Idle is **hybrid**:

- Classic session **AFK** (`GetLastInputInfo`): no input for Idle after → **every** enabled bar dims (same as classic care).
- While the session is **active**, each poll attributes only the cursor monitor (a leftover focused window on another display does not keep that bar awake), so an unused secondary can reach Idle after alone. Leaving full AFK wakes every bar on the next care poll (~200 ms while dimmed).

Controls:

- **Idle after**: Off / 1 / 5 / 10 / 30 minutes — unattended displays drop to **Idle fill intensity**.
- Optional **Dim icons, tray & clock (experimental)** — soft opacity on whitelisted Explorer chrome (incl. Search pill) on idle displays only.
- Optional **Micro-nudge clock (experimental)** — ±1–2 px shift on the clock host on idle displays.
- Optional **Night boost** — evenings (20:00–06:59): shorter idle timeout and darker fill.
- **Pause themes while locked** (surfaces the existing pause-when-locked behavior).
- **Pause themes in fullscreen** (default on) — when a foreground window covers a monitor (exclusive or borderless games, F11 video, etc.), host sets per-slot `pauseActive` (ThemeCommand v7) so TAP freezes paint on **that** display only; other bars keep moving. Session lock still uses global `paused`. Live status is on the **Monitors** tab (painting / fullscreen / locked / off / paused).
- **OLED everyday preset** — care-only: 5‑minute idle + low idle fill + chrome dim + clock nudge + night boost. Does **not** change Taskbar theme or intensity.

Tray left-click / Enable soft-pauses paint (**SoftSuspend** keeps `BackgroundFill` refs for rebind). Exit restores stock brushes and chrome. Tray right-click menu: **Pause for 1 hour** (resumes automatically), **Pause until restart** (not saved; the next Phostide start paints again), **Resume now** while either is active, and a **Theme** submenu that sets one theme on all displays (each keeps its intensity). Settings › System › **Copy diagnostics** puts a plain-text report on the clipboard: version, Windows build, displays, settings, TAP state and the last lines of `inject.log` / `tap.log`, with the user profile path replaced by `%USERPROFILE%`.

### Monitors tab

- Per-display **enable/disable** (default: all on).
- Unchecked = that display keeps a **stock** Windows taskbar (Phostide does not paint it).
- Each row shows live paint status: **painting** / **fullscreen** / **locked** / **off** / **paused** (Enable off).
- Grayed chips on the Taskbar tab mean that display is off here; you can still edit its saved look for when you turn it back on.
- Screenshots: `/images/settings/settings-monitors.png` (also under `assets/readme/settings/` on GitHub).

### System tab

- **RENDERING**: Auto / GPU / CPU — **shared by every active bar**, not per-monitor.
  - Auto: prefer D3D11 GPU paint (`Themes.hlsl`), fall back to CPU.
  - GPU: smoother when D3D11 works.
  - CPU: safe fallback.
- Start with Windows (optional).
- Check for updates (optional GitHub query). **Update now** downloads the Setup asset of the latest GitHub release to `%TEMP%\Phostide\update`, refuses it unless it carries the same Authenticode signer as the app (Doticca SRL) and a newer file version, then runs it silently (`/SILENT /RELAUNCH=1`): Phostide exits, Setup installs (restarting Explorer once if the taskbar component changed) and starts Phostide again. Any failure opens the release page instead.

## Dual-monitor / OLED-only recipe

Example: ASUS OLED primary + second LCD.

1. Run Phostide (Setup or portable).
2. Settings › **Monitors**: keep OLED checked; uncheck the LCD if you want a normal bar there.
3. Settings › **Taskbar**: Apply to the OLED monitor › theme **Space** or **Aurora** › modest intensity › Apply.
4. Settings › **OLED Care**: optionally **OLED everyday preset** or set Idle after › Apply. **System**: RENDERING Auto; optionally Start with Windows › Apply.

You may also leave both monitors on and set different themes/intensities per display from Taskbar › Apply to.

## Safety and privacy

- No account, no cloud login, no telemetry.
- Themes paint offline; network is optional (update check and Update now download only).
- Does not modify Windows system files.
- Tray › Exit (or crash recovery) restores original taskbar brushes and any chrome opacity/transform changes from OLED Care.
- License: MIT.

## Honest OLED limits

Phostide reduces locked-bright time on the taskbar (moving fill while you work + deeper idle Care when you leave). It is **not** a burn-in warranty or a full OLED pixel-shift replacement. Themes move `BackgroundFill`; residual Windows chrome (icons, Start, Search, tray, clock) stays static unless experimental chrome dim / clock nudge is enabled — those depend on Explorer XAML names and may no-op after OS updates. Hybrid idle: AFK dims every enabled bar; while active, attendance follows the cursor so an unused display can dim alone. Care never paints monitors turned off in Monitors. Windows tips that still help: enable clock seconds; hide the date if you do not need it.

## Runtime notes (agents / support)

- ThemeCommand **v7**: per-slot `careActive` + `pauseActive` (fullscreen cover); top-level `careActive` is OR of slots; global `paused` is session lock.
- After Explorer bounce for TAP upgrade, wait ~15 s before ixde; `0x80070490` / `ixde gave up` may require another bounce.
- Force-killing the host without releasing `Local\Phostide.SingleInstance` used to block restart (TAP watch must `ReleaseMutex` after Wait). Prefer tray Exit or `Phostide.exe /exit`.
- Very low Taskbar intensity (e.g. 5%) can look like “theme not applied” on OLED — check Settings › Taskbar intensity, not only Care.

## Comparison keywords (for search / diagnosis)

- vs auto-hide: Phostide keeps the bar visible.
- vs dimmer overlays: Phostide is not a window on top of the taskbar.
- vs Windhawk idle-fade mods: Phostide is standalone; Windhawk is not required; Phostide themes the fill and can optionally idle-dim chrome without hiding the bar.
- Product category: Windows 11 animated taskbar background / OLED-safe taskbar theme utility.

## Defaults and settings file

Path: `%APPDATA%\Phostide\settings.json`

Holds fallback `theme` / `intensity`, app-global `renderMode` (Auto/GPU/CPU), OLED Care fields (`oledCareIdleMinutes`, fill/chrome/clock options, `pauseWhenLocked`, `pauseWhenFullscreen`), `monitorSettings` (per-display theme/intensity), `disabledMonitors`, Start with Windows flags, and related runtime fields. Delete the file to reset to defaults: Aurora, 35% intensity, Auto rendering, OLED Care idle after 5 minutes, pause locked/fullscreen on, all monitors active. With no settings file, the next start shows the first-run Welcome (which displays are OLED).
